item.title: Trump is eager to declare victory, but a battered Iran still has cards to play
item.summary: The U.S. and Israel crippled Iranian forces in two weeks of war, but Tehran’s ability to disrupt oil flows and its uranium stockpile complicate the push to end it.

item.title: Trump urges world to help open Strait of Hormuz; U.S. Embassy in Baghdad hit
item.summary: The Pentagon identified the six service members who were killed when a U.S. refueling aircraft crashed in Iraq while supporting operations in Iran.

item.title: Trump says U.S. struck Kharg Island, core of Iran’s oil economy
item.summary: The strikes destroyed more than 90 military targets, including missile facilities, but preserved oil infrastructure, U.S. Central Command said Saturday.

item.title: GOP, fearing tough fight for Texas Senate seat, paints Democrat as radical
item.summary: Talarico, who is looking to flip Texas blue in his quest for the U.S. Senate, says the attacks from Republicans are a distraction from real issues.

item.title: Tracking who Trump is appointing to fill key administration roles
item.summary: Follow President Trump’s progress filling over 800 positions, among about 1,300 that require Senate confirmation, in this tracker from The Washington Post and the Partnership for Public Service.

item.title: Appointee wants to replace White House columns with the ones Trump prefers
item.summary: The head of a federal arts commission is proposing the more ornate Corinthian style for the nearly 200-year-old columns at the building’s front entrance.

item.title: White House proposes new visitor screening center to access grounds
item.summary: The 33,000-square-foot screening center, planned below Sherman Park, would be the Trump administration’s latest effort to remake the White House grounds.

item.title: Illinois Senate primary pits crypto-backed candidate against Pritzker’s pick
item.summary: The Democratic contest highlights divisions over crypto regulation and billionaire influence in politics, as the industry spends millions in a battle with the governor.

item.title: Push for GOP voting law has many switching sides on filibuster issue
item.summary: Some Republicans, just like Democrats in 2022, are eager to change the Senate’s rules in an effort to pass a national election law.
